chunks: Then look at the condition of your secretaries,
and appoint the best of them over your affairs.
and designate for your letters, in which you insert your policies and all your secrets, those who possess the best character, who are not elated by honor,
so that he dares not speak against you in common audiences regarding them,
and that negligence on his part does not cause him to fail in presenting the correspondence of your officials to you,
and in issuing correct replies to them on your behalf,
and in matters of what he collects for you and pays out from your funds,
and that he does not weaken a contract he has concluded for you,
and that he is not incapable of releasing what has been bound upon you,
and that he does not lack knowledge of the extent of his own capacity in affairs,
for indeed, he who is ignorant of his own position is even more ignorant of the position of others.
ai.seo_question: What qualities should a governor's secretaries possess according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This directive highlights the critical role of the *kuttab* (secretaries) as the administrative backbone of the Imamate, ensuring that state secrets and financial dealings are managed by those possessing *salamat al-din* (soundness of religion) and *salamat al-akhlaq* (moral integrity). It reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of spiritual virtue with administrative competence, warning against the arrogance that often accompanies power. The concluding maxim underscores the necessity of self-knowledge (*ma'rifat al-nafs*) as a prerequisite for just governance and accurate assessment of others.

en.sayed-ali-raza: (5. The Clerical Establishment) Then you should take care of your secretarial workers.
Put the best of them in charge of your affairs.
Entrust those of your letters which contain your policies and secrets to him who possesses the best character, who is not elated by honours,
lest he dares speak against you in common audiences.
He should also not be negligent in presenting the communications of your officers before you
and issuing correct replies to them on your behalf
and in matters of your receipts and payments.
He should not make any damaging agreement on your behalf
and should not fail in repudiating an agreement against you.
He should not be ignorant of the extent of his own position in matters
because he who is ignorant of his own position is (even) more ignorant of the position of others.
